title: Post-incident follow-up: multi-layer audit delivery gap caused by queue backpressure and key/signature mismatch during SSO token rekey
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a capacity spike on 2026-03-09 we observed a 47-minute window where tenant audit events were not delivered to the long-term audit sink. Root cause spans three interacting failures: (1) burst-driven backlog in the audit-aggregation layer caused bounded in-memory queues to drop events; (2) an HSM-backed key rotation job updated the signing key but a small subset of aggregator workers continued signing with the old key until process restart, causing signature verification failures at the sink; (3) an SSO token rekey run triggered mass session refreshes which amplified request volume and obscured observability signals. This ticket tracks remediation, backfill plan, and controls to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:03 UTC: Capacity spike begins after partner customer launched a large batch inference job (threefold traffic increase for 12 minutes).
2026-03-09 02:05 UTC: Audit aggregator queue length crosses soft limit; backpressure metrics warn but automatic shedding engaged and oldest-per-tenant events were dropped on overloaded shards.

2026-03-09 02:10 UTC: Scheduled HSM key rotation job runs. Most aggregator workers pick up new key via config push, but ~6% of workers fail to reload due to race in reload path and continue signing with old key.
2026-03-09 02:12 UTC: SSO rekey/rotation service returns new token secrets; clients begin session refreshes causing secondary traffic burst.
2026-03-09 02:15–03:02 UTC: Sink rejects a portion of audit batches due to signature verification mismatch; telemetry shows increased 4xx from sink and retries piled up.
root_cause: Compound failure: queue-size policy and metrics only signaled soft limits — not enforced backpressure routing to cold-storage; key rotation implementation lacked atomic key reference swap for all aggregator processes (reload race); SSO rekey created a correlated traffic spike. Individually each is recoverable, but combined they produced a cascade that led to dropped audit events and rejected batches.
action_items: A1: Make key rotation atomic across aggregator pool — implement leader-driven key reference swap and grace-period for signature verification. Owner: Luca Moretti. Due: 2026-03-28.
A2: Increase audit-aggregator durable buffering: wire in disk-backed spill-to-s3 queue for bursts > threshold. Owner: Eng infra (Jin Park). Due: 2026-04-09.
A3: Implement deterministic retry semantics with idempotent audit event IDs so rejected batches can be safely reingested without duplication. Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2026-04-02.
A4: Coordinate SSO rekeys with throttled session refresh cadence and circuit-breaker to avoid amplification; update runbook. Owner: Security eng (Marco Diaz). Due: 2026-03-21.

A5: Create cross-service observability dashboard that correlates queue-sizes, signature-verification-failures, and SSO refresh rates; alert on signature-mismatch rate > 1%. Owner: Observability team (Hannah Lee). Due: 2026-03-24.

A6: Backfill plan: identify dropped tenant ranges and reingest from ephemeral audit buffer and customer-facing logs. Phased run with verification checksums. Owner: Reliability (Aisha Patel). Due: 2026-03-31.
A7: Add canary rotation test that validates new signing key across a representative subset of aggregator instances pre-promote. Owner: Platform QA. Due: 2026-03-18.
follow_up_notes: 03/10: Initial postmortem draft reviewed by SecOps and Platform; agreed to treat as P0 and block release of next rotation job until A1 is implemented.
03/11: Runbook updated with immediate mitigations: temporary increase of in-memory queue to reduce dropping and manual throttling of partner batch jobs during rotation window.
03/12: Identified two tenants affected most severely; contacted customer success and provided CSV of missing event windows and planned reingest timeline.

03/13: Small hotfix merged to make key reload more deterministic — moves code path to single reload goroutine; rollout to canaries succeeded. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-aggregator/pull/427.
03/14: Observability query templates committed for cross-service incident response: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd-audit-incident
